note: Expand: create the trigger function that keeps amount and total in sync (whichever one a writer leaves NULL is copied from the other).
Expand: add nullable total (metadata-only) and the sync trigger in one transaction. Short lock_timeout with retries so we never queue app queries behind a waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock.

Backfill total from amount in 20k-row id batches, committing each batch (short row locks, no long transaction). Rows above the max id seen here were inserted after the trigger existed, so already have total.
Prepare NOT NULL on total: add a NOT VALID check constraint (brief lock, no scan), with lock retries.
Validate the check constraint: full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or writes. Fails (and stops the plan) if any row still has a NULL total.
Make total NOT NULL. Postgres uses the validated check constraint to skip the table scan, so the lock is brief; then drop the now-redundant check.
Switch the app to total. During the rolling update old pods write amount and new pods write total; the trigger fills the other column, so both versions keep working.

Contract: first wait until no client session's last query still uses amount (old app version), failing safely if one remains; then drop the trigger and the amount column in one transaction with lock retries, and drop the function.
